findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the 'Change 3351 does not interact' bullet: bridge fsck uses plain `run_git` rather than `run_git_bounded`, and the flaky test never invokes the CLI, so 3351 is irrelevant for that reason.
evidence: Plan: "it disables auto maintenance only for rebar's own bounded git children (`run_git_bounded`), and the CLI under test runs through those."
src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py:43 `from rebar._store.gitutil import run_git`; :94 `return run_git(  # raw-git-ok: bounded read-only grep/show of the committed tickets ref`
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:150-196 `run_git` is a thin subprocess.run wrapper and does not call `_without_implicit_maintenance` (only `run_git_bounded`/`run_git_reaped` do, lines 245/274)
tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev.py:246-268: the flaky test calls `_cli_tracker`, `_store_snapshot`, raw `git gc` and raw `git commit`, never `_run_cli`
findings.finding: The plan says the CLI under test runs through `run_git_bounded`, so change 3351's maintenance suppression covers it. That is false. bridge fsck's git calls go through plain `run_git` (no maintenance suppression) plus a raw `subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", ...])`. Also, the flaky test `test_store_snapshot_survives_git_maintenance_but_still_catches_mutation` never invokes the CLI. The conclusion that 3351 doesn't interact still holds, but for a different reason: the failing test makes no CLI call, and fsck only runs read-only grep/show, which don't spawn auto maintenance.
findings.location: Root cause (measured) — bullet 'Change 3351 (334295da063) does not interact'
scenarios: A later reader relies on this root-cause write-up to think bridge fsck's git children are maintenance-suppressed, when they run at git's defaults.
Someone checking the plan's exclusion of change 3351 finds the stated mechanism wrong and has to re-derive why the exclusion still holds.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the clause with: "Change 3351 (334295da063) does not interact: it suppresses auto maintenance only in `run_git_bounded`/`run_git_reaped`; the flaky test never invokes the CLI, and bridge fsck's own git calls (plain `run_git` grep/show, `rev-parse`) are read-only and spawn no auto maintenance. The daemon comes from the fixture's raw `git commit`."

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the positive control is made deterministic: isolate config (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointing to an empty file) and state the git version floor, or a skip condition when git is below that floor.
evidence: "A GIT_TRACE2_EVENT trace of that commit on this host (git 2.56.0)"
"as a positive control, the same trace mechanism records a `--detach` child for a repository built the same way without the pins"
No git version floor or config isolation is stated.
findings.finding: The positive control (an unpinned repository records a `--detach` child) depends on host state the plan does not control. It needs git at least 2.47, where maintenance.autoDetach and the `--detach` argument were introduced. It also needs no global or system config setting maintenance.auto, maintenance.autoDetach or gc.autoDetach to false. A CI host or developer machine with an older git or such config would fail the control.
scenarios: A CI runner with git 2.43 runs `git maintenance run --auto` without `--detach`, so the control assertion fails.
A developer has `maintenance.auto=false` globally, so no child is recorded and the control fails.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the minimum git version at which `git maintenance run --auto` carries `--detach`. Make `test_cli_tracker_leaves_no_detached_upkeep` skip with a reason below that version, or assert on a version-independent signal of detached upkeep.
evidence: "A GIT_TRACE2_EVENT trace of that commit on this host (git 2.56.0) records one child: `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`."
"as a positive control, the same trace mechanism records a `--detach` child for a repository built the same way without the pins"
Absence: the plan names no git-version floor or version-conditional skip for the trace assertions, and was measured on a single host/git version.

Platform fact: before git added the `--detach` option to `git maintenance run`, detachment of auto upkeep happened inside `gc --auto` (controlled by gc.autoDetach), with no `--detach` argument on the maintenance child.
findings.finding: The new test `test_cli_tracker_leaves_no_detached_upkeep` assumes that, without the pins, the fixture's `git commit` records a `git maintenance run` child carrying a literal `--detach` argument. That is true of recent git (the plan measured only git 2.56.0). Older git versions run `git maintenance run --auto` without a `--detach` argument and detach later, inside `gc --auto`, via `gc.autoDetach`. On those versions the positive control finds no `--detach` child and the test fails. The negative assertion would also pass vacuously, because the detaching process carries no `--detach` argument either. The plan states no minimum git version and no skip/guard.
scenarios: Linux CI runner on a distro-packaged older git (e.g. an LTS image): the positive control's `--detach` child is never recorded, so the new test fails red on an unchanged, correct fixture.

The same older-git host with the pins removed by a future regression: the negative assertion still passes, because the daemonizing process has no `--detach` argument, so the regression test does not catch the race it was written for.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the control repo is built inline in the test body (raw `git init` plus one commit, without apply_upkeep_pins), or explicitly allow a parameter on `_cli_tracker` and reconcile that with AC #3.

"No new config key, env var, flag or test helper is added."

scenarios: The executor adds `_build_tracker(pinned: bool)` to share fixture logic, which violates AC #3.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the control is built inline in `test_cli_tracker_leaves_no_detached_upkeep` with `git init` and `git commit --allow-empty`, without calling apply_upkeep_pins, and that no shared builder is introduced.

findings.finding: Step 2's positive control ('the same trace mechanism records a `--detach` child for a repository built the same way without the pins') can only be built two ways. One is to copy the `_cli_tracker` body (two git inits, user config, two `_write_event` calls, `_write_bindings`, prev_snapshot, add/commit), which duplicates the fixture. The other is to add a pin on/off parameter to `_cli_tracker`, which contradicts the plan's AC 'No new config key, env var, flag or test helper is added'. The codebase already has lighter, established positive controls for exactly this check, so the unpinned sibling repository is extra work that doesn't need to exist. It also depends on host git defaults: a host or global gitconfig that sets `maintenance.autoDetach=false` or `maintenance.auto=false` would make the control fail even though the fix is correct.
findings.location: Approach step 2 / Acceptance Criteria line 1 ('an unpinned control repository records one') vs AC line 3 ('No new ... flag or test helper')
scenarios: The implementer adds `pin: bool = True` to `_cli_tracker` to build the control, quietly breaking AC 3.
The implementer copies the fixture body into the new test. The two copies then drift, and the control stops being 'built the same way'.

findings.finding: The new test's positive control (an unpinned repository records a `--detach` maintenance child) depends on the host's global and system git config. A CI or developer machine whose ~/.gitconfig or /etc/gitconfig sets maintenance.autoDetach=false, gc.autoDetach=false or maintenance.auto=false will record no `--detach` child, and the control fails spuriously. Without a hostile global config, the pinned half of the test also never shows that the local pins override a global autoDetach=true.
scenarios: A host with `maintenance.auto=false` or `maintenance.autoDetach=false` in its global gitconfig: the control repository records no --detach child, so the new test fails on a correct fix
A host whose global config leaves autoDetach at its default: the pinned assertion passes, but nothing shows that local pins beat a global autoDetach=true

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the pinned case, assert that exactly one `git maintenance run --auto` child is recorded and that its argv contains the `--no-detach` token (not merely that no child has `--detach`).
evidence: "assert ... that no recorded `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`"
Taxonomy item 5 (missing cardinality assertion) and item 4 (fixture invalidity): an absence-only assertion has no positive anchor.
findings.finding: The pinned-fixture assertion ('no recorded git maintenance run child carries --detach') passes vacuously when no maintenance child is recorded at all. That happens if GIT_TRACE2_EVENT is not propagated into the fixture's git subprocesses, or if the trace file is empty. The positive control runs on a different repository, so it does not rule this out for the fixture.
scenarios: The fixture builds its git env without inheriting GIT_TRACE2_EVENT, so the trace captures nothing and the test passes even with the pins removed.
findings.suggested_fix: For the pinned fixture, assert `len(children) == 1`. Then assert `'--no-detach' in argv` and `'--detach' not in argv`, using argv token equality rather than substring matching.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the exact stress command (e.g. `for i in $(seq 200); do pytest -n 4 tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev.py -q || exit 1; done`) and state that the trace test, not the stress run, is the discriminating proof.
evidence: "The flaky test and the rest of the module pass 200 consecutive runs under `pytest -n 4`."
"Run alone it passed 6/6." / "which is why it shows only under `make verify`"
findings.finding: The 200-consecutive-runs AC names no command. Running repeats needs pytest-repeat's `--count` (possibly a new dependency) or a shell loop. The plan also does not show that this stress run fails without the fix: the flake was seen only under full `make verify` load, and the test passed when run alone.
scenarios: The executor adds pytest-repeat to run `--count 200`, which conflicts with the no-new-tooling intent.
The 200 runs pass both before and after the fix, so the AC proves nothing about the race.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a shell loop over `pytest -n 4 tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev.py` that exits on the first failure. Note that the mechanism is proven by `test_cli_tracker_leaves_no_detached_upkeep`, and that the stress run is supporting evidence only.

That happens if the trace was not written for that build, if the env did not reach the commit, or if auto-maintenance was disabled.
